storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk this evening — skies are clear, radar is empty, and it stays dry and breezy, so the cove gets the same quiet weather as the surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer in play: air and Sound water are both about 66°F at 4 PM, and the air cools to the mid-50s by 8 PM — colder than the water — so the Sound isn't changing anything tonight.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: a dry, post-frontal northwest flow covers the whole area. The 3:51 PM radar scan shows no storm cells anywhere in range, there are no National Weather Service alerts, and the forecast is simply "Sunny" with a gusty northwest wind.

No fuel for storms: the atmosphere's storm energy (CAPE) is zero now and stays zero through the evening in the forecast model. Winds aloft are strong — about 68 kt of wind change between the surface and 6 km — but without any instability that only shows up as a gusty breeze, not as thunderstorms.

Local effect — not in play: the cove's usual protection comes from a layer of cool air sitting over the Sound when the water is much cooler than the land. Today there is no gap to work with: the water is 66°F and the inland air is 66°F at 4 PM. As the sun sets (6:29 PM) the air cools quickly while the Sound holds its temperature, so by 6 PM the air is about 7°F colder than the water and by 8 PM about 13°F colder. That is the reverse of the protective setup, and there is no sea breeze either — only 1 of 15 coastal stations shows any southerly wind.

Most likely outcome: a dry, clear, cooling evening for the cove, identical to surrounding areas. The only weather to plan around is the wind — still gusting in the mid-to-upper 20s kt at the Riverside YC station at 4 PM — which eases steadily after sunset.

What would change the call: nothing on the horizon for tonight. It would take showers appearing on radar upstream to the west or northwest, which neither the model nor the forecast suggests.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient wind — gusty west-northwest, no sea breeze in play

hourly.shift_note: gusty and puffy, big oscillations off the land
slight right shift, gusts settling after sunset

wind.tactics_blurb: Gusty west-northwest wind blowing off the land — puffy and shifty early, easing steadily after the 6:29 PM sunset. No side pays consistently: stay center, tack on the headers, and keep out of the holes close under the western shore.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: this is a moderate gradient-wind day — the wind is driven by the large-scale weather pattern, not by a sea breeze. The air–water temperature difference is essentially zero (inland air 66°F, Sound 66°F), so there is no thermal engine, and only 1 of 15 coastal stations shows any southerly flow. The well-sited airport anemometers average 13 kt from the west-northwest.

Right now in the cove: the Riverside YC station read west at 16 kt gusting 28 at 4 PM, with an 18.5 kt ten-minute average — noticeably stronger than the forecast model's 13 kt for the same hour. The early hours of the table are nudged up to reflect that; the model's easing trend is kept.

Will it hold: yes in direction, no in strength. A gradient wind does not shut off at sunset the way a sea breeze does, but the gusts are fed by daytime mixing, and that ends as the air cools (68°F at 4 PM to the mid-50s by 8 PM). Expect roughly 15 kt gusting 25 at 5 PM, about 10 kt around sunset, and 5–7 kt by 8–10 PM, staying west-northwest throughout (285–300°).

Where the pressure is: west-northwest wind reaches the course over Belle Haven and Field Point, so it arrives in puffs with holes between them, and the holes are worst tight under the western shore. Better average pressure sits mid-cove and toward the mouth. The model shows a small right shift toward 300° around 7 PM and then a swing back left to about 287° by 8 PM — not enough of a one-way trend to commit to a side, which is why the center is the call.

Shift character: oscillating, with large swings (15–30°) riding in on the puffs — typical for wind off the land. Nearby stations confirm the patchiness: only 59% of the network agrees on direction, with sheltered inland stations light and variable while the open-water readings are strong and steady.

What the fleet feels: 5 PM is a big-breeze, hike-hard start for dinghies with gusts in the mid-20s; by 6–7 PM it is powered-up but manageable at 9–11 kt; after 8 PM it is light air at 5–7 kt and fading, with the last hour at risk of going patchy near shore.

data_caveats: The forecast model (HRRR 3 PM run) only reached 8 PM at fetch time; the 9 PM and 10 PM wind rows are extrapolated from its trend, not model output.
The 5–7 PM wind speeds are nudged above the model because the Riverside YC station was reading about 5 kt stronger than the model at 4 PM.
The forecast model has no gust data; gust figures are estimates scaled from current Riverside YC and airport gusts.
Buoy 44040 (western Sound) observation is 90 minutes old and was excluded from the live wind picture.
Westchester airport (KHPN) wind sensor is down; its temperature is still used as the inland reference.

Wind direction agreement across the station network is low (59%), mostly from sheltered inland stations reading light and variable — typical of a gusty wind off the land rather than a sign of a front.
